editorial_validation.scope: Dune, Dune Messiah and Children of Dune, with major book spoilers announced. The entire story means Paul's life as told in those three original novels. No expanded prequels, fictional intervening adventures, or scene details imported from the films.

review_findings_before_final_local_edits.quote: To survive the attempt, Paul needs the riding technique Stilgar and his people teach him.
review_findings_before_final_local_edits.reason: H18 identifies a point restated with nothing new attached. The preceding sentence already explains that Paul must understand precisely how a Fremen survives the encounter, and the following paragraphs identify the teaching and technique concretely.

review_findings_before_final_local_edits.quote: The crisis comes when Chani's death provides the circumstance for the implanted command to kill Paul. For Hayt, carrying out that command would mean murdering the person Duncan Idaho had died defending. The conflict is unbearable, and Duncan's memories return through it. His recovered identity matters because he resists the act demanded of him. The Tleilaxu conditioning meets a loyalty rooted in his earlier life, and that loyalty becomes active again. Paul survives this intended attack because the person within Hayt refuses to complete it.
review_findings_before_final_local_edits.reason: This paragraph advances to the childbirth climax, after which chapters 20 and 21 return to the pregnancy and stone burner without a marked retrospective handoff. Chapter 22 repeats the same crisis and resistance in their chronological home. H18 says a repeated observation should have one home paragraph; deletion here preserves all substantive developments later.

review_findings_before_final_local_edits.quote: The recovery changes what the Tleilaxu can offer Paul. Before this moment, they could return a body with familiar features and new training. Now Duncan's awakening demonstrates that personal memories can return as well. For a man facing bereavement, that is a terrible discovery to receive from an enemy. Duncan is genuinely restored to him, and the restoration gives the Tleilaxu a stronger means of applying pressure. Paul has regained someone who can remember him as the young Atreides heir. He must also live with knowing that the people who arranged their reunion intended to use that love against him.
review_findings_before_final_local_edits.reason: This advances beyond Hayt's arrival to the consequence of his recovered identity, which chapter 22 explains again through Scytale's concrete offer concerning Chani. Under H18, the later version adds the actual demand and is the more useful home. Removing this paragraph together with the preceding finding leaves chapter 19 ending coherently on the danger of Hayt's conditioning.

review_findings_before_final_local_edits.quote: Paul is among those injured, even as his conduct begins to make him seem separate from them.
review_findings_before_final_local_edits.reason: H18 applies because the paragraph has already said that Paul suffers the same bodily loss as other victims, while both the opening and next paragraph explain his unusual conduct. This sentence adds neither a new injury nor a new consequence.

review_findings_before_final_local_edits.quote: Leto's rise also means that Muad'Dib can remain useful after the Preacher has been killed. The new ruler is Paul's son. His descent gives Paul's name a continuing place in the succession, alongside the religious life already built around it. Paul has become part of the ancestry through which the next government is understood. His public name can be spoken in accounts of legitimate succession even though the man himself had returned to attack the order governing under that name.
review_findings_before_final_local_edits.reason: H18 identifies repeated framing without sufficient new development. The preceding paragraph has already established succession through the surviving children, and the final paragraph gives the stronger concrete endpoint through Arrakeen's temple, officials and Atreides descent. This intervening paragraph makes the ending land twice.
